title: Lesson 1: Completing the Whole - Fast Addition Trick
learningGoals: Understand that every number has a complement that completes a round whole.
Use complement thinking to complete numbers mentally.
coreIdeas: A complement is the missing part needed to reach a round whole like 10, 100, or 1000.
Look for the missing part first instead of counting one by one.
The same complement idea scales from 10 to 100 to 1000.

workedExamples.method: Think: what is missing from 7 to reach 10? The missing part is 3.

starterPractice: Warm-up: What is the complement of 7 to make 10?

onboarding.coachIntro: Today you will learn how numbers complete a whole like 10, 100 and 1000.
onboarding.placementRule: If the learner answers complement pairs to 10 instantly, start from complements to 100.

mission.missionPromise: Master complements to 10, 100 and 1000 and complete numbers at lightning speed.
mission.successCelebration: Amazing! You can now spot the missing part to a whole in seconds.

microLessonPattern: Coach names the sutra and gives one punchy example.
Board shows the rule visually with colour highlights.
Student reads the rule aloud before trying.
Student attempts the question before the answer appears.

Review prompt checks if the student can state the rule from memory.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: What is a complement?
sessionFlow.coachHook: A complement is the missing part that completes a whole. If 7 needs 3 to make 10, then 3 is the complement of 7 to 10.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Show 7 + 3 = 10 and 6 + 4 = 10 with the missing part highlighted.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: What number joins with 3 to make 10?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: what joins with 8 to make 10?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: Say the complement of 6 to make 10.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes. You found the missing part to make the whole.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Think: 8 + ? = 10. Count up to the whole.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick fire: complements of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 to make 10.
